Can VeIR parse these LLVM operations?

Full measurement ↗

LLVM operationStrictAllow unregisteredInput & diagnostics

Each row groups reference-verified cases in generic MLIR syntax, with VeIR verification disabled. Parsed means all recorded cases parsed and printed successfully. Partial means some cases parse and others do not; expand the row to see which. These samples do not cover every syntax or type variant. Rejected locates the first parser error at the named operation. Blocked means surrounding code, a type or an attribute failed first. Allowing unregistered operations can preserve them as opaque operations; it does not establish their verification or execution support.

Category counts measure operations with at least one parsed example; case counts measure depth separately. Categories are disjoint: llvm.intr.experimental.* is experimental, other llvm.intr.* operations are intrinsics, and the remaining operations form the core group, including functions, globals and structural operations. This naming-based split is not a commitment to support every category.
